# Reception Perception: The Show — 2024-01-30

**Raw transcript:** `raw/ingested/reception-perception/2024-01-30-rp-conference-championship-review-more-coaching-hires.md` (immutable — do not edit)

## Summary

With co-host **James Koh** (not tracked). Two halves: a Conference Championship
recap (Chiefs over Ravens, 49ers over Lions — both games already covered from
the Waldman side in [[Matt Waldman's RSP Cast - 2024-01-29]]) and a run through
several fresh head-coaching/coordinator hires.

**AFC Championship.** [[Patrick Mahomes]] gets an "annoyed" defense of a
counting-stats-light win (77% completion, 100 passer rating) plus a
skeptical read on whether Kansas City can repeat this formula with an
unaddressed receiver room. [[Travis Kelce]] gets an emphatic reinforcement —
11-for-11 targets, "rumors of his demise were greatly exaggerated," worth
remembering "next season" regardless of a quiet regular-season stretch.
[[Lamar Jackson]] gets Harmon's most critical read of him yet: three
turnover-worthy throws (a specific bad decision into triple coverage
targeting Isaiah Likely, not given a page), an abandoned run game (Ravens'
design-run rate ranked 563rd of 568 games played league-wide this season),
and an explicit open question about "playoff losses mounting" — while still
being called a top-three quarterback outright. [[Zay Flowers]] gets a
rookie-arc framing around a goal-line fumble (worst 115-yard/TD game
possible) but real "star potential" language for a receiver room the hosts
think still needs more talent around him. [[Rashad Bateman]] gets a mixed
update — made it through the year healthy, "flashes" liked, but not yet a
"key contributor" without more added around him. [[Jared Goff]]'s Ben
Johnson-to-Washington rumor firms further ("worst kept secret in the
league"), with new context that OL coach Hank Fraley may follow Johnson out
the door.

**NFC Championship / draft-value follow-up.** [[Jameson Williams]] gets
light third-party corroboration of the post-game optimism from Waldman's
prior episode — Harmon flags the pre-draft trade-up as a fair miss so far
but tempers the criticism given the two-touchdown Championship game.

**Coaching-hire fallout, filtered for player relevance** (per this wiki's
low-durability-on-coaching-churn-alone standard, only hires directly tied to
a specific player's projected role are ingested; general coordinator-bio
discussion for Atlanta's Zach Robinson, Carolina's Dan Morgan promotion, and
Detroit's defensive staff is not):
- **Atlanta hires Zach Robinson (Rams OC) under new HC Raheem Morris.**
  Harmon expects a man-heavy/gap run scheme translated from the Rams,
  projected as a good mechanical fit for [[Bijan Robinson]] (with
  [[Tyler Allgeier]] still mixed in as a complementary piece) and for
  [[Drake London]] on Puka-Nacua/Cooper-Kupp-style in-breaking routes.
- **Tampa Bay loses OC Dave Canales to Carolina (new HC).** Directly
  threatens the offensive infrastructure credited with "unleashing"
  [[Mike Evans]] and finally solving [[Chris Godwin]]'s optimal role in
  2023 — flagged as a fresh, live 2024 variable for both, and for
  [[Baker Mayfield]] himself, whose own game got attributed largely to
  Canales's scheme design. Canales's Carolina arrival also produces the
  episode's most extended single-player breakdown: a new page for
  [[Bryce Young]], graded as physically limited (below-average arm,
  undersized, not especially elusive) such that his only real path to
  success is a hyper-accurate, high-processing game — with the rookie
  season's badness attributed to bad line play, bad weapons and a bad
  scheme fit under Frank Reich rather than settled on talent alone.
- **Philadelphia hires Kellen Moore (ex-Cowboys/Chargers OC).** Extends
  the already-open [[Jalen Hurts]] variable from the prior Waldman episode
  with an actual (mixed/tepid) grade — real under-center/play-action
  question given how shotgun-exclusive Hurts's usage has been, some
  optimism on Moore's ability to scheme easy completions, explicit note
  that Philadelphia's bigger problem is a lack of complementary weapons
  beyond A.J. Brown/DeVonta Smith (not tracked pages).

## Not given pages

Isaiah Likely and Mark Andrews (injury/target mentions only, no standalone
evaluative read), Odell Beckham Jr. and Nelson Agholor (free-agency mentions
only), Kadarius Tony (locker-room-drama mention, no football evaluation),
Michael Pittman Jr. (dismissed in passing — "don't get your hopes up" on him
changing teams), Kyren Williams (brief scheme-fit mention, no new
evaluative content beyond what's already on his page), A.J. Brown, DeVonta
Smith and Dallas Goedert (named only as existing Eagles pieces, no
individual evaluation given). Steve Spagnuolo, Mike Macdonald, Zach
Robinson's coaching bio, Raheem Morris, and Dan Morgan's promotion are
out of scope — coaching-carousel detail with no specific player
role/usage attached beyond what's captured above.
